comparison: Perfect agreement on TEM dynamics claims (C6, C47-C50). Both evaluations find the evidence supported, with peer reviewers specifically praising the work for 'pinning down the key role of caveolin-1' and distinguishing it from cavin-1 effects. OpenEval notes the mechanism remains to be elucidated, which aligns with peer acknowledgment that 'its mechanism remains to be further investigated.'

Perfect agreement on in vivo mouse survival experiments (C7, C52-C55, C64, C95). Both find the evidence supported. Peer reviewers praise the 'comprehensive' approach including in vivo work. OpenEval notes the direct link to TEM formation in vivo remains inferential, but both accept the findings as valid.

Strong agreement on membrane mechanics and tether pulling experiments (C8, C56-C60, C65-C67, C78, C91). Both evaluations find evidence supported. OpenEval notes the 30% vs 55% discrepancy between experiment and theory. Peer reviewers describe the biophysical approach as 'rigorous' and 'compelling,' contributing to 'very convincing' conclusions.

Strong agreement on theoretical modeling (C2, C21-C22, C79, C87). Both find the theoretical framework supported. Peer reviewers explicitly validate the approach, calling the dewetting analogy 'very attractive' and noting STORM data supports key assumptions. OpenEval notes some assumptions may be oversimplified, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'the validity of the Helfrich formalism is a key assumption' but accept it as supported.

Both address caveolae-TEM relationship claims with substantial overlap (C3-C4, C35-C37). OpenEval finds strong support from quantitative imaging with large sample sizes. Peer reviewers affirm this as an 'important study' with 'rigorous and compelling' evidence. Peer result R1 also covers additional claims (C30-C34, C61-C62) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Both address electron microscopy data on caveolae density (C30-C31, C62). OpenEval finds the quantitative EM measurements well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers include these claims in their overall positive assessment of the caveolae-TEM findings as 'rigorous and compelling.'

Both address protein depletion effects (C32-C34). OpenEval finds immunoblot data supported but notes cross-depletion complicates interpretation. Peer reviewers include these claims in their overall affirmation of the study's findings without specific critique of the cross-depletion issue.

Both address cell morphology changes (C5, C41-C46, C63, C80). OpenEval finds strong support from quantitative measurements of area, volume, and height. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the 'very convincing' accumulation of evidence. Peer result R2 also covers actin-related claims (C38-C40, C77) that OpenEval addresses separately in R4.

Both address actin cytoskeleton observations (C38-C40, C77). OpenEval finds STORM imaging data supported and notes the negative finding (no exacerbation) is important for ruling out cytoskeletal mechanisms. Peer reviewers specifically praise 'the quality of STORM images (Fig. 2) which are very illuminating' and support the conclusions.

Strong agreement on background/contextual claims (C1, C9-C29, C97-C98). Both evaluations find these established knowledge claims supported by appropriate citations. OpenEval notes these provide essential context but are not novel findings. Peer reviewers do not question these background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

Both address literature-based mechanistic context (C69-C74). OpenEval finds these supported by appropriate citations providing context for interpretation. Peer reviewers rate these as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the hypotheses as 'very plausible though challenging' but noting 'the mechanism remains to be further investigated.' Peer result R7 also includes speculative claim C75 that OpenEval addresses separately in R12.

Both address speculative mechanistic hypotheses (C75, C85 in OpenEval). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative and lack direct experimental support. Peer reviewers similarly rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'we may feel slightly frustrated by the absence of data in this direction' while acknowledging the hypotheses are 'very plausible though challenging.'

Both address the theory-experiment discrepancy explanation (C68). OpenEval finds the explanation reasonable but suggests the theoretical framework may need refinement. Peer reviewers accept the model while acknowledging key assumptions, noting STORM data now supports the Helfrich formalism assumption.

Both address integrated mechanistic conclusions (C88-C91). OpenEval finds the integration of findings into a coherent model supported. Peer reviewers accept these conclusions as part of the overall 'very convincing' evidence, specifically noting the work distinguishes caveolin-1's role 'as an individual protein instead of the main molecular component of caveolae.'

Partial overlap on membrane mechanics conclusions (C90-C91). OpenEval finds the mechanistic integration supported. Peer reviewers affirm the biophysical evidence as 'rigorous' and contributing to 'very convincing' conclusions about caveolin-1's role.

Both address cell volume regulation claims (C83-C84). OpenEval finds the volume measurements supported and notes the independence from RhoA is novel. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the comprehensive evidence without specific comment on the RhoA independence.

Both address the main summary claim (C61). OpenEval finds it accurately summarizes findings supported by multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers include this in their overall affirmation, describing the study as 'important' and the conclusions as 'very convincing.'

Both address host-pathogen interaction context (C92-C93, C96, C99). OpenEval finds these supported by citations and experimental data, noting bidirectional effects and complexity. Peer reviewers do not specifically critique these contextual claims, accepting them as part of the established background.

Both address fundamental physical principles (C86). OpenEval finds this principle supported by experimental observations linking cell height to TEM frequency. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on this principle but accept the overall physical framework as valid.

Minimal overlap on volume regulation context (C81-C82). OpenEval finds these supported by citations and volume measurements. Peer reviewers include these as part of accepted background without specific evaluation.
